subChunks.title: ORDER BY and LIMIT
subChunks.hookHtml: SQL doesn't promise any row order. "Top 5 by XP" only makes sense when you explicitly sort first — then take five.
subChunks.explanationHtml:
ORDER BY

SELECT name, xp FROM apprentices ORDER BY xp;        -- ascending (default)
SELECT name, xp FROM apprentices ORDER BY xp DESC;   -- descending
SELECT name, rank, xp FROM apprentices ORDER BY rank, xp DESC; -- multi-column

Multi-column sort: rows are first grouped by rank; ties are broken by xp DESC.

LIMIT

SELECT name, xp FROM apprentices ORDER BY xp DESC LIMIT 3;

Always pair LIMIT with ORDER BY. Without ORDER BY, "top 3" could be any 3 rows the engine happens to return — the result is non-deterministic.

Clause order

SELECT columns
FROM   table
WHERE  condition
ORDER BY columns
LIMIT  n;

Clauses must appear in this written order even though the engine evaluates FROM → WHERE → SELECT → ORDER BY → LIMIT internally.

storyBeats.text: The Headmaster sends a runner — he wants the three highest-XP apprentices posted on the Hall board by noon.

storyBeats.speaker: Cipher the Archivist
storyBeats.text: ORDER BY xp DESC puts the highest XP first. LIMIT 3 takes the first three. Without the ORDER BY, 'three apprentices' means any three — not the top three. Never LIMIT without ORDER BY.

subChunks.feynmanPrompt: Explain why LIMIT without ORDER BY is almost always a bug, using the apprentices leaderboard as an example.

questions.prompt: What does `ORDER BY xp` (no keyword after) do?
options: Throws a syntax error — ASC or DESC is required
questions.explanation: Ascending is the default. ORDER BY xp and ORDER BY xp ASC are equivalent. To reverse, add DESC.

questions.prompt: What does `SELECT name FROM apprentices ORDER BY xp DESC LIMIT 2` return from the lesson data?
questions.explanation: Sorted by xp descending: Elara 7500, Cassia 4800, Bjorn 2400, … LIMIT 2 takes the first two: Elara and Cassia.

questions.prompt: Which clause ordering is syntactically valid SQL?
options: SELECT → FROM → WHERE → ORDER BY → LIMIT
SELECT → WHERE → FROM → ORDER BY → LIMIT
SELECT → FROM → ORDER BY → WHERE → LIMIT
SELECT → LIMIT → FROM → WHERE → ORDER BY
questions.answer: SELECT → FROM → WHERE → ORDER BY → LIMIT
questions.explanation: SQL clause order is fixed by the grammar. You must write them in this sequence even though the engine evaluates them in a different internal order.

questions.prompt: A junior writes `SELECT name FROM apprentices LIMIT 5`. What is the problem?
options: No ORDER BY — the five rows returned could be any five, not the first five in any meaningful sense
LIMIT requires a WHERE clause to be valid
SELECT name returns only one column so LIMIT is redundant
LIMIT 5 always returns the same 5 rows so it is harmless
questions.answer: No ORDER BY — the five rows returned could be any five, not the first five in any meaningful sense
questions.explanation: Without ORDER BY, the relational model makes no row-order guarantee. Different engines, different query plans, even different executions can return different rows. LIMIT without ORDER BY gives non-deterministic results.
